title: Normality of smooth lattice polytopes
statement_utf8: Is every smooth lattice polytope normal? For a $d$-dimensional lattice polytope $P$, “smooth” means that the normal fan of $P$ consists of unimodular cones, while “normal” means that every lattice point in $kP$ is the sum of $k$ lattice points in $P$ for every $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every dimension and every positive dilation; smoothness and normality explicitly defined.
technical_assessment: Triangulating all smooth polytopes unimodularly is a stronger unsupplied bridge. Dimension-specific normality checks cannot settle the unbounded question; no full-scope route.

title: Conjecture 2: Remainder estimates for Liouville tori
statement_utf8:
Let $M$ be a torus with a Liouville metric. Then
\[
R(\lambda)=O\!\left(\lambda^{\frac12+\varepsilon}\right),\qquad R_x(\lambda)=O\!\left(\lambda^{\frac12+\varepsilon}\right),\qquad N_{x,y}(\lambda)=O\!\left(\lambda^{\frac12+\varepsilon}\right),
\]
for any $\varepsilon>0$ and for all $x\ne y\in M$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All epsilon>0 and distinct points, but R,R_x,N_x,y and spectral normalization are absent.
technical_assessment: Lattice counting for an arbitrary Liouville metric needs metric-dependent oscillatory estimates; cannot replace the three unidentified remainders with one standard Weyl remainder.

title: Decay of linear waves on Schwarzschild spacetime
statement_utf8: Let $(M,g)$ be Schwarzschild, let $S$ be an arbitrary Cauchy surface for $(M,g)$, and let $\\phi$ be the unique solution of the wave equation $\Box_g\phi=0$ on $(M,g)$ with sufficiently regular, compactly supported initial data prescribed on $S$. No symmetry is assumed on $\\phi$. Understand the decay properties of $\\phi$ in $R=J^{+}(\mathcal I^{-}_{A})\cap J^{-}(\mathcal I^{+}_{A})$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every compact-data solution is mentioned, but no decay rate, norm or asymptotic endpoint is requested.
technical_assessment: Energy decay and pointwise Price-law asymptotics are different targets; specifying either would invent a replacement statement. Park without a certificate.

title: Attainment of the one-dimensional sharp Strichartz constant
statement_utf8:
For the one-dimensional Strichartz inequality
\[
\|u\|_{L^6_{t,x}(\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R})}\le S\,\|u_0\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})},
\]
the best constant \(S>0\) is attained. The report further states that
\[
S=12^{-1/12},
\]
and that a corresponding minimizer/maximizer is \(u_*(x)=e^{-|x|^2}\), together with all its images under the symmetry group.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: The evolution defining u from u_0 and its time normalization are omitted.
technical_assessment: Gaussian extremizers and the displayed constant are stated as report results; checking a Gaussian alone cannot prove global optimality. Likely known-result route, body clearance absent.

title: Global well-posedness for the one-dimensional defocusing quintic NLS at and below the energy regularity
statement_utf8:
For the defocusing quintic nonlinear Schrödinger Cauchy problem
\[
 i\partial_t u+\Delta u=|u|^4u,\qquad u(x,0)=u_0(x),\qquad x\in\mathbb R,
\]
is the problem globally well-posed in time for every initial datum in the Sobolev spaces \(H^s(\mathbb R)\) with \(s\ge 0\) for which the local theory is valid?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every H^s datum for s>=0 admitting local theory for the explicit defocusing PDE.
technical_assessment: Mass-critical global control requires concentration/compactness and spacetime bounds; conservation of mass alone does not iterate the critical local theory. No short full-scope mechanism.

title: Examples attaining the lower bound for the \b6-order
statement_utf8: For every prime $p$, do there exist a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a finite group $G$, and a nonzero Tate cohomology class $[\zeta]\in \widehat{H}^{n}(G,k)$ of even degree $n$, represented by a map $\zeta:\Omega^{n}k\to k$, such that $\zeta\text{-ord}(k/\zeta)=p-2$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every prime p; existential field, finite group and even-degree class; zeta-order and k/zeta undefined.
technical_assessment: Cyclic-group Tate classes might test orders but the triangulated-category order definition is indispensable; p=2 alone is not full scope.

title: Weak limiting behavior of cuts needed to isolate the root of a random recursive tree
statement_utf8:
Let $T_n$ be a uniformly distributed random recursive tree with $n$ vertices, and let $X_n$ be the number of random edge cuts needed to isolate its root. Then, as $n\to\infty$, $\frac{\log^2 n}{n}X_n-\log n-\log\log n\xrightarrow{d}X$, where $X$ is a $1$-stable random variable with characteristic function
\[
\mathbb{E}(e^{itX})=e^{it\log|t|-\frac{\pi}{2}|t|},\qquad t\in\mathbb{R}.
\]
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Distributional limit is precise but the random cutting protocol is unspecified.
technical_assessment: Uniformly choosing surviving edges and choosing original edges give different experiments; stable-law convergence is not certified by expectations or simulations. No new theorem claimed.

title: Generic nefness and pseudo-effectivity of the canonical bundle
statement_utf8: Let $X$ be a projective manifold of dimension $n$. A line bundle $L$ on $X$ is generically nef if $L\cdot H_1\cdots H_{n-1}\ge 0$ for all ample line bundles $H_1,\ldots,H_{n-1}$. Suppose $K_X$ is generically nef. Is $K_X$ pseudo-effective?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every projective manifold with the stated intersection inequalities for all ample tuples.
technical_assessment: Duality with movable curves tests more than complete intersections on X; replacing movable tests by ample tuples is the unresolved bridge. Surface cases do not settle all dimensions.

title: Dolbeault cohomology of nilmanifolds with left-invariant complex structure
statement_utf8: For every nilmanifold $M=\Gamma\backslash G$ with left-invariant complex structure $J$, can the Dolbeault cohomology $H^{p,q}(M,J)$, for all bidegrees $(p,q)$, be calculated using left-invariant differential forms?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All nilmanifolds with invariant complex structure and every bidegree.
technical_assessment: Nomizu's de Rham argument does not automatically compute Dolbeault cohomology; rationality and holomorphic torus filtrations need additional hypotheses. No uniform mechanism.

title: Small deformations of nilmanifolds with left-invariant complex structure
statement_utf8: For every nilmanifold $M=\Gamma\backslash G$ with a left-invariant complex structure $J$, are all sufficiently small deformations of $(M,J)$ again nilmanifolds with left-invariant complex structures?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every invariant complex nilmanifold and all sufficiently small complex deformations.
technical_assessment: Invariant differential graded deformation models require a cohomology comparison not supplied uniformly. The adjacent Dolbeault question cannot be used as a proved dependency.

title: Nonvanishing critical Voronoi rectangle-crossing probability
statement_utf8: In planar Voronoi percolation at the critical parameter $p=1/2$, let $h(\rho,s)$ be the probability that there is a black path crossing the rectangle $[0,\rho s]\times[0,s]$ horizontally. For every $\rho>1$, $$\limsup_{s\to\infty} h(\rho,s)>0.$$
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every aspect ratio rho>1; positive limsup of critical Voronoi horizontal crossings.
technical_assessment: A Russo-Seymour-Welsh crossing theorem would subsume this weaker limsup, but an exact applicable body/version must be checked before a prior-defeat assertion. No new route proposed.

title: RSW-type a priori crossing bound for anisotropic critical percolation
statement_utf8: For bond percolation on the square lattice with horizontal and vertical edge-open probabilities $p_h$ and $p_v$, respectively, satisfying $p_h+p_v=1$, does there exist a constant $c>0$ such that $\mathbb{P}(H(n,n))\ge c$ for every $n$, where $H(a,b)$ is the event that $[0,a]\times[0,b]$ has an open horizontal crossing?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All n with p_h+p_v=1; parameter endpoints and crossing convention are not specified.
technical_assessment: At p_h=0,p_v=1 horizontal crossing fails under the usual convention. This is an excluded domain correction, not a substantive discovery; interior anisotropic crossing bounds require real percolation input.

title: Relation between an overpartition rank-difference function and Hurwitz class numbers
statement_utf8:
Theorem 3 ([5]) states that

$$f(-q)=-16H(q)-\frac{1}{3}\Theta^3(z).$$

Here the report defines $f(q)=\sum_n\alpha(n)q^n=\sum_n(p_e(n)-p_o(n))q^n$ using the even- and odd-rank overpartition counts, and $H(q)=-\frac{1}{12}+\sum_{n\ge1\atop n\equiv0,3\pmod4}H(-n)q^n$ using Hurwitz class numbers.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: A generating-function identity is supplied but Theta and its variable relation to q are undefined.
technical_assessment: Literal text labels this Theorem 3; coefficient tests could expose normalization issues but cannot convert a stated theorem into new credit. No primary proof audit.

title: Theory of the tilt-angle phenomenon for non-Newtonian liquids
statement_utf8: “There is until now no satisfactory theory to explain the tilt angle phenomenon for non-Newtonian liquids.” Here, the tilt angle is the angle formed by the long axis of symmetry of a falling cylinder or ellipsoid with the horizontal; experimentally, it may range from $0^\circ$ to $90^\circ$ depending on the particle and liquid properties.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: An experimental lack-of-theory observation without constitutive equation or mathematical target.
technical_assessment: No universal quantified proposition is available; fitting tilt angles or choosing a fluid law would replace the question. Retain missing-scope row.

title: Normalizer property for groups with finite normal subgroups satisfying NP
statement_utf8:
The normalizer problem (NP) for a group $G$ asks whether the normalizer of $G$ in the unit group of $
\mathbb{Z}G$ consists only of the obvious units, namely the subgroup generated by $G$ and the central units of $
\mathbb{Z}G$. If (NP) holds for every finite normal subgroup of $G$, does (NP) hold for $G$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All groups G satisfying NP for every finite normal subgroup.
technical_assessment: Finite-support units do not imply the subgroup they generate is finite normal; a reduction to such a subgroup is an unproved bridge. No bounded counterexample family identified.

title: Derived-series subgroups from commutator powers of augmentation ideals
statement_utf8:
Let $G$ be a free group. For a commutative ring $R$, let $\Delta(G)=\Delta_R(G)$ denote the augmentation ideal of $RG$, set $\delta_1(RG)=[\Delta(G),\Delta(G)]_{RG}$, and define $\delta_{n+1}(RG)=[\delta_n(RG),\delta_n(RG)]_{RG}$ for all $n\in\mathbb N$. If $G^{[n]}$ denotes the $n$-th term of the derived series of $G$, is it true that
$$
G\cap\bigl(1+\delta_n(\mathbb ZG)\bigr)=G^{[n]}?
$$
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All free groups and derived indices; the ring commutator subscript does not specify additive subgroup versus generated ideal.
technical_assessment: These operations differ and alter the dimension-subgroup intersection. Magnus expansion at finitely many degrees cannot prove the universal integral equality; definition must be recovered first.

title: Shellability of the space of tropically collinear points
statement_utf8: Develin conjectured that the tropical variety $T_{d,n}$ of the determinantal ideal generated by the $3\times3$ minors of a $d\times n$ matrix is shellable for all $d$ and $n$. The report states that this conjecture is proved.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All d,n but fan/complex realizing shellability is not fixed.
technical_assessment: The literal already says the report proves the conjecture. Shellability is a property of a chosen complex, not merely its support; no new outcome or body clearance claimed.

title: Maximality of the real Zeuthen problem for two lines
statement_utf8: For every integer $d\ge 2$, does there exist a configuration $C$ of $2$ real lines and $d(d+3)/2-2$ real points such that all degree-$d$ curves passing through the points and tangent to the lines are real, equivalently $$N_d^{\mathbb{R}}(2,C)=N_d(2)?$$ The report answers this affirmatively.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every d>=2; existential real configuration but enumerative genericity and complex counting convention omitted.
technical_assessment: Literal announces an affirmative report answer. Degenerate configurations cannot refute the intended enumerative statement; existing constructive proof must be read before investment.

title: Independence numbers of arbitrary powers of odd cycles
statement_utf8: The problem of determining the independence numbers of arbitrary powers of odd cycles remains widely open.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Arbitrary odd cycles and powers, but graph product/power operation unspecified.
technical_assessment: Ordinary distance powers and strong powers have different independence problems. No parameter enumeration before fixing the operation; retain without replacement.

title: Kalai’s Conjecture A for centrally symmetric polytopes
statement_utf8:
For every centrally symmetric convex polytope $P$ of dimension $d$, with $f_i(P)$ denoting its number of $i$-dimensional faces, one has
$$
\sum_{i=0}^{d} f_i(P)\ge 3^d.
$$
The report states that this conjecture is open for $d\ge 5$ (and holds for $d\le 4$).
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every centrally symmetric d-polytope; counts nonempty faces including P.
technical_assessment: Crosspolytopes and cubes realize equality. Checking them does not constrain arbitrary face lattices. Same underlying 3^d family as 394918, never two credits.

title: Kalai’s 3^d-conjecture for centrally symmetric polytopes
statement_utf8: For every centrally symmetric convex $d$-polytope $P$ with $d\ge 5$, the total number of nonempty faces satisfies $\displaystyle\sum_{i=0}^{d} f_i(P)\ge 3^d$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every centrally symmetric d-polytope for d>=5 and every nonempty face dimension.
technical_assessment: Same total-face lower bound as 394917 restricted to the hard dimensions; no full-scope argument, no separate-family proposal.

title: Question 1: Collapse-forcing-invariant models of ZFC
statement_utf8: Does there exist a model $N$ of ZFC such that, for every cardinal $\\lambda$ of $N$ and every generic subset $H$ of $\\operatorname{Col}(\\omega,\\lambda)$, one has $N[H] \\equiv N$? Here $\\operatorname{Col}(\\omega,\\lambda)$ is the forcing to collapse $\\lambda$ onto $\\omega$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Existential ZFC model; all its cardinals and collapse generics; external generic availability/model semantics unstated.
technical_assessment: Forcing invariance may require consistency assumptions and a transitive or countable model convention; vacuous absence of generics is not an eligible counterexample.

title: Higher-level separation of projective measurability and the Baire property
statement_utf8: Can we prove a variant of Theorem 6, where the set without the Baire property is a $\[1m\Delta^1_{k+1}\u001b[0m$ set, and we have, in addition, the Baire property for all $\[1m\Sigma^1_k\u001b[0m$ sets, $k\ge 3$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All k>=3 is stated but the referenced Theorem 6 and its consistency hypotheses are missing.
technical_assessment: A projective separation construction cannot be specified from these clauses alone; garbled formatting also retained literally. No reconstructed replacement claim.

title: Dimension of the p-rank-zero locus in the Siegel moduli space with Iwahori level structure
statement_utf8:
For the Siegel moduli space $\mathcal A_{g,I}$ with Iwahori level structure at $p$, the dimension of its $p$-rank-$0$ locus is conjectured to be
$$\left\lfloor\frac{g^2}{2}\right\rfloor$$
for every integer $g\ge 1.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every g>=1; Iwahori Siegel p-rank-zero locus, but precise integral model and base fiber absent.
technical_assessment: Affine-Weyl stratum dimensions could compute examples, not the universal maximum over admissible strata. Missing model and prime conventions block full fidelity.

title: Characterizing bounded universality for self-maps of non-simply connected domains
statement_utf8: Characterize, for a non-simply connected planar domain \(\Omega\), those sequences \((\phi_n)\) of self-maps of \(\Omega\) for which there exists a \(B\)-universal function, where \(B=\{f\in H^\infty(\Omega):\sup_{z\in\Omega}|f(z)|\le 1\}\) and \(f\in B\) is \(B\)-universal for \((\phi_n)\) when \(\{f\circ\phi_n:n\in\mathbb N\}\) is locally uniformly dense in \(B\).
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every nonsimply connected planar domain and sequence of holomorphic self-maps; B and local-uniform density defined.
technical_assessment: Classification must cover multiply connected domains with both trivial and nontrivial bounded function algebras; disk universality criteria cannot simply be transported. No full criterion.

title: Global attraction of finite-energy solutions to the solitary-wave set
statement_utf8: A natural hypothesis is that the set of all solitary waves forms a global attractor for all finite-energy solutions.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All finite-energy solutions but no evolution equation, topology or solitary-wave definition.
technical_assessment: Global attraction in local topology differs from energy-norm attraction; radiation rules out naive strong convergence but not the unspecified statement. No proposal.

title: Massless-photon and point-charge limit of the nonrelativistic QED g-factor formula
statement_utf8: Does (14) have a finite limit when $m_{\mathrm{ph}}\to 0$ and $\widehat{\varphi}(k)\to (2\pi)^{-3/2}$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Massless and point-charge limits refer to absent formula (14).
technical_assessment: Joint and iterated limits may differ and renormalization matters. Cannot calculate a limit without the actual integrand and dependencies.

title: Local injectivity of the Carmichael \-function
statement_utf8: For every positive integer $m$, there is an integer $n\ne m$ such that $\lambda(n)=\lambda(m)$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every positive integer m has a distinct positive integer sharing Carmichael lambda.
technical_assessment: Odd m has lambda(2m)=lambda(m); many even cases reduce similarly, but this does not supply a uniform construction for all prime-power lcm patterns. Inspect primary for known full result before investment. Actual printed p688 explicitly retains an enormous-effective-threshold gap in the unconditional route; stop rather than a finite sweep.

primary_passage.coverage: Printed p688: unconditional target; ERH result and a remaining prime-power/Pratt-tree obstruction. No proof body of Ford-Luca read.

title: Conjectured optimal order of the primitive of Hardy’s function
statement_utf8: Let $Z(t)=\chi^{-1/2}(\tfrac12+it)\zeta(\tfrac12+it)$ be Hardy’s function and let $F(T)=\int_0^T Z(t)\,dt$. Ivić conjectured that the estimate $F(T)\ll T^{1/4+\varepsilon}$ for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$ is close to being best possible.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every fixed epsilon>0, but close to best possible is not an explicit lower-bound quantifier.
technical_assessment: An Omega result, failure of power saving, and the upper estimate itself are distinct obligations. Do not turn a heuristic optimality phrase into a theorem target.

title: Almost-prime solutions to ternary quadratic equations
statement_utf8: Let $g(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ be an indefinite anisotropic quadratic form with determinant $d(g)$, and let $t\ne 0$ be an integer such that $d(g)t$ is square-free. The reported result states that the equation $g(x_1,x_2,x_3)=t$ has infinitely many solutions for which the product $x_1x_2x_3$ has at most $26$ prime divisors. Under Selberg’s eigenvalue conjecture, the bound $26$ can be reduced to $22$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All indefinite anisotropic ternary forms and square-free d(g)t; solution ring and local representability absent.
technical_assessment: Congruence obstructions can make the stated equation insoluble; original sieve theorem must include representation hypotheses. A local-obstruction example would be a scope correction only.

title: Positive density of prescribed digit sums of squares
statement_utf8:
Let $q\ge 2$ be an integer, and write $\sigma(n)$ for the sum of the base-$q$ digits of $n$. For every integer $m\ge 2$ with $(m,q-1)=1$, there exist constants $C(q,m)>0$ and $x_0(q,m)\ge 1$ such that, for every $a\in\mathbb Z$ and every $x\ge x_0(q,m)$, 
$$
\#\{n\le x:\ \sigma(n^2)\equiv a\pmod m\}\ge C(q,m)x.
$$
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every base q>=2 and coprime modulus m>=2; uniform in residue a and all sufficiently large real x.
technical_assessment: Digit-block constructions may give sublinear families; positive linear density needs carry and distribution estimates, not one representative per residue. No full-density route.

title: Maximum antichain size in the divisor poset of an integer
statement_utf8: Let $p_1,\ldots,p_N$ be distinct primes and let $M=p_1^{k_1}\cdots p_N^{k_N}$, where $k_i\ge 1$. Identify the set $D$ of divisors of $M$ with $\prod_{i=1}^N\{0,1,\ldots,k_i\}$, ordered by divisibility (equivalently, coordinatewise order). What is the maximal size of a subset $A\subset D$ such that, for every distinct $r,r'\in A$, neither $r\mid r'$ nor $r'\mid r$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All products of finite chains with positive exponents; asks exact largest antichain.
technical_assessment: Classical symmetric-chain decomposition gives the middle coefficient of product(1+x+...+x^k_i). This is a routine known-poset application, ineligible even if the source presents it as a problem.

primary_passage.coverage: Printed pp806-807: divisor antichain passage, weighted probability context and Sperner discussion. Whole report not read.

title: Critical almost Mathieu spectrum Hausdorff-dimension conjecture
statement_utf8:
For every $\[?1m\alpha\u001b[0m \in \mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$, does the critical almost Mathieu spectrum satisfy
$$
\dim_H\bigl(S(\alpha,2)\bigr)<\frac12?
$$
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every irrational alpha but the almost-Mathieu operator defining S(alpha,2) is absent.
technical_assessment: Strict less-than-half is stronger than a non-strict upper bound; small rational approximants are neither spectra at irrational frequency nor proofs of Hausdorff dimension. No exact route.

title: Uniqueness of two Majorana representations of $A_5$
statement_utf8: The alternating group $A_5$ of degree five possesses exactly two Majorana representations, of dimensions $26$ and $21$, corresponding respectively to $(2A,3A,5A)$- and $(2A,3C,5A)$-subgroups in the Monster that are isomorphic to $A_5$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Exactly two Majorana representations of A5; axioms and representation equivalence omitted.
technical_assessment: An algebra dimension check cannot classify all Majorana structures. Monster realizations supply candidates, not uniqueness absent the source axioms.

title: Sylow-subgroup characterization of the soluble radical
statement_utf8: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $p$ be a prime, and let $P\in\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)$. Then $P\subseteq\operatorname{sol}(G)$ if and only if $\langle P,g\rangle$ is soluble for all $g\in G$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All finite groups, primes and Sylow p-subgroups; equivalence with every one-element extension soluble.
technical_assessment: Forward direction follows from radical normality and soluble cyclic quotient; reverse direction requires a finite-group recognition theorem. No elementary full-scope proof supplied.

title: Babai’s diameter conjecture for finite non-abelian simple groups
statement_utf8:
For every non-abelian finite simple group $G$ and every generating set $A$ of $G$, there exist absolute constants $c$ and an implied constant such that
\[
\operatorname{diam}(\Gamma(G,A)) \ll (\log |G|)^c,
\]
where $|G|$ is the number of elements of $G$.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Uniform absolute constants across all finite nonabelian simple groups and generating sets are intended.
technical_assessment: Product-growth bounds for bounded rank do not give the required rank-uniform polylogarithmic diameter. Fixed-group BFS is a parameter helper only.

title: Does a codistance on a 2-spherical building imply a twinning?
statement_utf8: For every 2-spherical building $\mathcal B$, does the existence of a codistance on $\mathcal B$ imply that $\mathcal B$ is one half of a twin building (equivalently, that the codistance extends to a twinning)?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All 2-spherical buildings; codistance and twinning axioms not stated.
technical_assessment: A local codistance extension need not glue globally without connectivity/extension arguments; no finite certificate or full-scope construction identified.

title: Classification of $(d,4)$-nets
statement_utf8: Conjecture. The only $(d,4)$-net is the Hesse arrangement of 12 lines.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Only Hesse arrangement claimed, but base field, degeneracies, net definition and equivalence absent.
technical_assessment: Real versus complex fields materially change existence. Small line-arrangement solving without these conventions would test another statement.

title: Regularity of fibers of general projections
statement_utf8: Work over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Let $X\subset \mathbf P^r$ be a smooth projective variety of dimension $n$, and let $\pi:X\to\mathbf P^{n+c}$ be a general projection, with $c\ge 1$. Is it true that, for every $y\in\mathbf P^{n+c}$, $\operatorname{reg}(\pi^{-1}(y))\le \frac{n}{c}+1$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All smooth char-zero projective X, c>=1, general projection and every target point y.
technical_assessment: The ceiling/floor interpretation is forced by integral regularity, but arbitrary nonreduced special fibers need control. Generic reduced fibers alone do not settle every y.

title: Equality with the normalization of the reduced coarse moduli space
statement_utf8: Is $M_{1,n}(m)=\widetilde{M}_{1,n}(m)$ for all $m$, where $\widetilde{M}_{1,n}(m)$ is the normalization of the reduced space $M_{1,n}(m)$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All m but the moduli functor M_1,n(m), allowable indices and base field omitted.
technical_assessment: Normality is a local deformation-ring question; normalization notation alone cannot specify the objects. Park rather than invent an elliptic-moduli model.

title: Short Presentation Conjecture for Finite Groups
statement_utf8: Every finite group $G$ has a presentation whose length is $O\bigl((\log |G|)^3\bigr)$; the report states that this bound is best possible.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All finite groups and absolute asymptotic bound; length encoding omitted.
technical_assessment: Bit-length and relator-letter length differ on powers; known short-presentation results must be matched to the actual encoding. No fresh mechanism.

primary_passage.coverage: Printed p1543: explicitly distinguishes length from bit length; report dependency only.

title: Cohomology-dimension bounds for absolutely irreducible modules
statement_utf8: For each integer $j>0$, there is a constant $C_j$ such that, for every finite group $G$, every field $k$, and every absolutely irreducible $kG$-module $M$, $$\dim H^j(G,M) \le C_j(\dim M)^{j-1}.$$
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: For each j>0 uniform C_j over all finite groups, fields and absolutely irreducible modules.
technical_assessment: For j=2, trivial modules over elementary abelian p-groups have unbounded second cohomology. This is a classical omitted-group-scope obstruction; source likely restricts groups. No discovery credit from correcting it.

primary_passage.coverage: Printed pp1543-1544: Corollary E explicitly assumes faithful; next conjecture prints the unqualified statement. No corrected universal assertion adopted.

title: Ore's conjecture
statement_utf8: Every element of every finite nonabelian simple group is a commutator.
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every element of every finite nonabelian simple group.
technical_assessment: Ore is a recognized solved conjecture; finite classification and character estimates are substantial existing dependencies. Read exact body before asserting source-level resolution, never propose as fresh.

primary_passage.coverage: Printed pp1548-1550: Theorem3 says Ore holds in general; proof strategy and computational base discussed, full dependency paper not read.

title: The fake degree conjecture for algebra groups at odd primes
statement_utf8: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $P=1+A$ be a finite algebra group, equipped with its classical Cayley map and associated co-adjoint orbit set $\mathcal O$. Then the fake degree conjecture holds: for every $k\ge 0$, \[\{\chi\in\operatorname{Irr}(P):\chi(1)=p^k\}=\{\Omega\in\mathcal O:|\Omega|=p^{2k}\}.\]
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All odd p, algebra groups and k>=0; literal equality compares characters with orbits instead of cardinalities.
technical_assessment: The displayed sets have different kinds of elements; intended cardinality assertion and Cayley hypotheses must be checked. Type/wording correction earns no credit.

primary_passage.coverage: Printed p1560: reports affirmative odd-prime algebra-group result; typesetting of orbit equality is unreliable; no proof body audited.

title: Euler-characteristic target enumeration
statement_utf8:
Given a finite collection of tame target supports $\{U_\alpha\}\subset X$ with uniform Euler characteristic $\chi(U_\alpha)=N\ne 0$ for every $\alpha$, and counting function $h:X\to\mathbb{N}$, the number of targets is
\[
\#\alpha=\frac{1}{N}\int_X h\,d\chi.
\]
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Finite tame supports of equal nonzero Euler characteristic; h is not required to count membership.
technical_assessment: The formula follows immediately by Euler-integral additivity if h=sum of indicators. Without that link arbitrary h refutes the wording only; neither route yields eligible novelty.

primary_passage.coverage: Printed pp1620-1621: counting function explicitly counts active supports; Theorem1 and its entire short additive proof read.

title: De Giorgi’s conjecture for the Allen–Cahn equation in dimensions up to eight
statement_utf8:
For dimensions $N\le 8$, let $u$ be a bounded solution of
$$
\Delta u+(1-u^2)u=0\quad\text{in }\mathbb{R}^N,
$$
with $\partial_{x_N}u>0$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$. Is it true that, for every $\lambda$, the level set $\{x\in\mathbb{R}^N:u(x)=\lambda\}$ is a hyperplane?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every bounded monotone entire solution N<=8 and every real lambda, including values outside its range.
technical_assessment: Empty level sets outside (-1,1) defeat literal hyperplane wording but are an excluded endpoint correction. Intended one-dimensionality in dimensions 4..8 has no short full-scope mechanism here.

title: Existence of minimizing Willmore surfaces of prescribed genus
statement_utf8:
For every $q\in\mathbb{N}_0$, there exists a smooth Willmore embedding $f:\Sigma\to\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\operatorname{genus}(\Sigma)=q$ and $W(f)=\beta_q$, where
\[
\beta_q=\inf\{W(f)\mid f:\Sigma\to\mathbb{R}^n\text{ smooth, closed immersion, }\operatorname{genus}(\Sigma)=q\}.
\]
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Every genus; ambient dimension n and Willmore energy normalization are not quantified/defined.
technical_assessment: Smooth minimizing embeddings require compactness and exclusion of bubbling; low-genus explicit surfaces cannot prove the all-genus statement. No bounded route.

title: Almost-everywhere convergence of bilinear ergodic averages for two arbitrary commuting transformations
statement_utf8:
Let $(X,\text{probability space})$ be a probability space, let $S$ and $T$ be commuting but otherwise arbitrary measure-preserving transformations of $X$, and let $f,g$ be bounded measurable functions. Is it true that, for almost every $x\in X$, the averages

$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} f(T^n x)g(S^n x)$$

converge as $N\to\infty$?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All probability spaces, commuting measure-preserving S,T, bounded f,g; almost everywhere as N tends infinity.
technical_assessment: Norm convergence and diagonal S=T theorems do not imply pointwise convergence for arbitrary commuting pairs. No maximal inequality route established.

title: Conjectured optimal weight range for Bergman projections over light-cone tubes
statement_utf8:
Let $T=\mathbb{R}^{d+1}+i\Omega$ be the tube domain over the open light-cone, with Lorentz form $Q(y)=y_0^2-|y'|^2$. The weighted Bergman projections $P_\gamma$ are conjectured to be bounded on $L^p\bigl(T^{d+1},Q(y)^\gamma\,dx\,dy\bigr)$ for every $\gamma>-1$ throughout the range
\[
1+\frac{d-1}{2(\gamma+d+1)}<p<1+\frac{2(\gamma+d+1)}{d-1}.
\]
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: All gamma>-1 and displayed p interval; d range, cone sheet and projection kernel conventions missing.
technical_assessment: The d=1 denominator flags an omitted dimension restriction; an endpoint objection is a domain correction only. Cone multiplier estimates remain major dependencies.

title: Prime entries in determinant-two matrices
statement_utf8:
Is the set of $2\times 2$ matrices with determinant $2$ and all four entries prime infinite? Equivalently, is
$$\{A=(a_{ij})\in M_2(\mathbb Z): \det A=2,\ a_{11},a_{12},a_{21},a_{22}\text{ are prime}\}\
$$
infinite?
classification_reason_and_quantifiers: Infinitely many positive-prime-entry integer 2x2 matrices with determinant exactly 2.
technical_assessment: Matrix [[3,7],[7,17]] is one witness, not infinitude. Fixing three entries reduces to simultaneous prime linear forms, where Dirichlet alone is insufficient; no uniform construction.
